findings.title: Naive body extraction can duplicate required sections after a Markdown horizontal rule
findings.claim: Naive rendered-body splitting can hide required headings after a Markdown horizontal rule and append duplicates.
findings.suggested_fix: Use crate::item_text::split and add a structured-body horizontal-rule regression.
findings.evidence: The previous split matched both the closing frontmatter delimiter and an ordinary Markdown horizontal rule. The canonical item_text splitter now preserves the full body, and the custom-schema regression proves Expected is emitted once.

findings.title: Structured-body renderer lacked an adjacent unit test
findings.claim: The changed structured-body renderer branch lacked an adjacent core unit test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a write.rs unit test for wrapper suppression and source placement.
findings.evidence: Before the review fix, write.rs test constructors only set structured_body=false and no test exercised the true branch. The new renderer test now passes and pins exact source/body placement.

findings.title: Shipped issue template contradicted body-file behavior
findings.target_symbol: Action: Create / Flesh out the body
findings.claim: The shipped issue template contradicted itself about whether body-file creates a Description wrapper.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify minimal-body behavior by input mode and document schema-required stubs.
findings.evidence: The template's body-file paragraph said no wrapper while the later create step unconditionally listed Description. Both source formats and dogfooded copies now carry conditional wording.

findings.title: User-visible fix lacked an Unreleased changelog entry
findings.claim: The user-visible body-file fix lacked an Unreleased changelog entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a concise Fixed bullet through the curated changelog workflow.
findings.evidence: The initial diff changed persisted CLI output but did not touch the marked Unreleased section. A Fixed bullet has now been added under the approved curated changelog contract.

findings.title: Intake body-file structured-versus-free-text semantics are unresolved
findings.claim: Intake file body-file still uses free-text wrapping and may duplicate a supplied Description heading.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide whether intake body-file is free text under a generated section or structured Markdown, then align help, skills, and tests.
findings.write_up:
- **Milloin tämä näkyy käyttäjälle** — kun intake-raportti annetaan `--body-file`-tiedostona ja sisältö on jo jäsennelty H2-otsikoilla.
- **Miten se näkyy** — intake käsittelee tiedoston vapaana tekstinä ja lisää oman `## Description` -otsikkonsa; tiedostossa jo oleva sama otsikko voi siksi kahdentua.
- **Miksi sillä on väliä** — intake on agenteille suositeltu vastaanottopolku, joten epäselvä sopimus tuottaa eri rakenteen kuin saman niminen `create --body-file` -valitsin.
- **Mistä päätös on kyse** — säilytetäänkö intaken nykyinen vastaanottorakenne, jossa raportti sijoitetaan generoituun kuvausosioon, vai määritelläänkö tiedostosyöte jäsennellyksi Markdowniksi kuten create-komennossa.
- Päätös vaatii erillisen yhteensopivuus- ja dokumentointiarvion; tämän tehtävän nimenomainen create-rajaus säilyttää nykyisen intake-käytöksen.
findings.evidence: dispatch_intake collapses body_file into FileRequest.body, and intake::file explicitly constructs NewArgs with structured_body=false. This is real behavior, but intake help calls the body free text and the requested task explicitly preserves other creation paths.

findings.title: Boolean body mode permits contradictory core states
findings.claim: Option description plus a structured-body Boolean permits contradictory core states.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the fields with an InitialBody enum.
findings.evidence: The core type can represent structured_body=true with no description, but the CLI cannot produce it because empty body files are rejected. Replacing the model would coordinate many callers without demonstrated real-world failure in this bounded path.

findings.title: Plain-prose body-file behavior is an unintended regression
findings.claim: Suppressing the wrapper for plain-prose body files is an unintended compatibility regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Sniff content or add a separate structured-body flag.
findings.evidence: The verified contract defines body-file as structured Markdown placed directly below the generated preamble. Deterministic source-mode semantics are intentional; content sniffing would make behavior formatting-dependent.
